title: Run-rate and ops-efficiency scenario sheet for private deployments
content: Purpose: Quick, numeric-first worksheet to compare run-rate economics and operational efficiency levers for Private deployments (customer-managed: on-prem purchase, on-prem lease, vs VPC-hosted private subscription). This sheet is meant to feed recommendations for licensing + support bundle packaging and minimum scale guidance for sales.
content_rows:
ASSUMPTIONS
- Analysis horizon: 3 years (annualized costs shown).
- Baseline workload: steady-state 10M inference requests/month (70 token average; use simplified token-hours).
- GPU equivalent: 8x A100-80GB class (for on-prem purchase).
- Asset life (purchase): 4 years; lease term: 36 months.
- Staff: 1.0 FTE infra engineer + 0.3 FTE support/ops for on-prem; 0.2 FTE for VPC (customer-managed roles reduced).
- Power & DC: conservative estimate for colocation.
- License tiers modeled: Core (no 24/7), Enterprise (24/7 L1 + SLA), Enterprise-Plus (24/7 + proactive optimization + managed patching).

SCENARIOS SUMMARY TABLE
Columns: Scenario | Upfront capex | Annualized capex | Annual ops | License+support | Staff (annual) | Power+DC | Total annual cost | Equivalent $/million requests

Row: On-prem purchase | $1,200,000 | $300,000 | $60,000 | $120,000 | $220,000 | $48,000 | $848,000 | $84.80
(Notes: Upfront capex includes GPUs, servers, NVMe, networking. Annual ops includes maintenance contract + spare pool.)

Row: On-prem lease (36mo) | $0 upfront | $420,000 | $60,000 | $132,000 | $220,000 | $48,000 | $880,000 | $88.00
(Notes: Lease includes hardware replacement SLA; higher annual run cost, reduced capital risk.)

Row: VPC subscription (private region) | $0 upfront | $0 | $780,000 | $240,000 | $90,000 | $12,000 | $1,122,000 | $112.20
(Notes: VPC subscription priced as cloud equivalent reserved capacity + software license; includes some managed ops. Staff counts are lower but license/support is higher.)

Row: VPC reserved blocks + lite support | $0 upfront | $0 | $540,000 | $96,000 | $120,000 | $12,000 | $768,000 | $76.80
(Notes: Lower support tier and larger reserved commitment; requires more customer-side ops.)

SENSITIVITY: Utilization impact on $/M requests (On-prem purchase baseline)
Utilization | Effective available inference-hours/month | Total annual cost (annualized) | $/M requests
30% | 2,160 hours (lower eff) | $848,000 | $139.67
50% | 3,600 hours | $848,000 | $83.90
70% | 5,040 hours | $848,000 | $59.86
90% | 6,480 hours | $848,000 | $46.59
(Interpretation: On-prem purchase only wins at sustained high utilization > ~60% assuming baseline load; below that, Opex models or VPC reserved blocks look cheaper.)

ADD-ON & LICENSE BREAKDOWN (annual)
- Core: $48,000 (basic software, limited telemetry).
- Enterprise: $120,000 (SLA, 8x8 response, security reviews).
- Enterprise-Plus: $240,000 (SLA, 24x7 NOC, monthly optimization reports, patch management).
- Managed Ops add-on (optional): $96,000/year (1:1 runbook + on-call rotation + quarterly capacity reviews).

LEVERED COSTS: Example bundle combos (annual totals)
- On-prem purchase + Enterprise support + managed ops: total = $848k (see table).
- On-prem purchase + Core license, no managed ops: total = $776k -> lowers customer price but higher ops risk.
- VPC + Enterprise-Plus (managed): total = $1.122M.
- VPC + reserved blocks + Core: total = $768k (competitively priced if customer handles more ops).

COST DRIVERS & SENSITIVITY NOTES
- Hardware amortization: single biggest swing for purchase vs lease. Shorter asset life (3 yrs) increases annualized capex by ~33%.
- Utilization: non-linear effect on $/inference. Small increases in average utilization deliver outsized unit-cost reductions for on-prem owned hardware.
- Support SLAs: moving from Core -> Enterprise-Plus can add 2–3x incremental license spend but reduces staff burden and incident resolution time.
- Overprovisioning penalty: 10–25% idle buffer required for patching/maintenance increases effective cost; include in proposals.
- Migration buffer: recommend 15% additional capacity in year 1 for migration spikes (affects purchase economics).

SIMPLE BREAKEVEN RULE OF THUMB (annualized)
- If expected steady-state monthly inference requests < 8M and customer unwilling to operate >0.5 FTE, VPC reserved or subscription is likely lower total cost of ownership.
- If sustained monthly requests > 12M and customer commits to 1+ FTE for ops, on-prem purchase begins to be attractive (assuming 4yr asset life and stable workload).

QUALITATIVE RISK MATRIX (short)
- On-prem purchase: Risk: Hardware EOL, staffing churn, capacity mis-forecast; Benefit: Lowest unit cost at high utilization, full data control.
- On-prem lease: Risk: higher run-rate, but lower capital risk; Benefit: predictable replacement, reduced ops surprise.
- VPC subscription: Risk: higher license/ops fees and vendor lock-in; Benefit: fastest time-to-scale, minimal local ops, built-in fallbacks and regional redundancy.

RECOMMENDATIONS (actionable for packaging + go-to-market)
1) Create two default commercial bundles for Private:
   - "Ops-Light VPC" (target: <10M/mo) = reserved compute blocks + Core license + optional L2 support. Price to match $/M requests ~ $80–95 at target scale.
   - "Enterprise Self-Host" (target: >=12M/mo) = On-prem purchase amortized 4yrs + Enterprise license + managed ops optional. Include guidance on minimum FTE and utilization thresholds.
2) Add a "Hybrid lease" offering in sales playbook for risk-averse accounts: 36mo lease + Enterprise license + 1yr managed ops included.
3) Introduce utilization-based credits in the contract: if customer average utilization < 40% for 6 months, offer an operational review and potential reserved-to-lease conversion.
4) Pricing collateral: show 3-year total run-rate waterfall (capex amortization, license, ops, staff, power) and highlight sensitivity bands for +/-20% utilization.

NEXT STEPS (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- Validate cost inputs with infra-finance: confirm colo rate and power numbers (target by 2024-11-15).
- Run Monte Carlo sensitivity (Lina Chen) over utilization and asset-life assumptions (due 2024-11-22).
- Draft two customer-facing one-pagers mapping bundle to expected cost per 1M requests for sales (Devon Miller).
- Pilot lease offer with 2 mid-market customers to validate pricing (Q1 2025).

NOTES & OPEN QUESTIONS
- Need actual A100-equivalent list+discount pricing from sourcing to firm capex numbers.
- Is there appetite from legal for utilization-linked contract clauses? (tag legal)
- Confirm if the managed ops add-on will include on-call for customer-facing incidents or only advisory.

CHANGELOG
- 2024-11-03: Initial draft with baseline numbers (Marco).
- 2024-11-12: Added VPC reserved-block scenario (Aisha).
- 2025-02-12: Tuned staff assumptions and added recommendation to pilot lease (Lina).
